### Page note: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_660
Reader state: complete; relevance: partial
The supplied page is an excerpt from the Wikipedia article on NVIDIA’s **GeForce 600 series**. It contains a detailed table that lists each GPU in the series along with launch dates, code‑names, die details, and most importantly, the size of the memory bus (the “Bus Width” column). For every GPU listed, the table provides the value of the memory bus width in bits.

**Page**  
GeForce 600 series – https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_660  
(Excerpt from the “Products” / “Chipset table” section)

**Evidence**  

| GPU | Launch | Code‑name | Transistors (M) | Die Size (mm²) | Bus Width (bits) | Notes |
|-----|--------|-----------|-----------------|---------------|------------------|-------|
| **GT 630** | April 24 2012 | GK107 | 1 300 | 118 | **128** | 1 024 MiB GDDR5 |
| **GT 660** | September 13 2012 | GK106‑400‑A1 | 5 850 | 220 | **192** | 2 048 MiB GDDR5 |
| **GT 660 Ti** | August 16 2012 | GK104‑300‑KD‑A2 | 7 200 | 250 | **192** | 2 048 MiB GDDR5 |
| **GT 670** | May 10 2012 | GK104‑325‑A2 | 7 500 | 280 | **192** | 4 096 MiB GDDR5 |
| **GT 680** | March 22 2012 | GK104‑400‑A2 | 8 000 | 320 | **192** | 4 096 MiB GDDR5 |
| **GT 690** | April 29 2012 | 2×GK104‑355‑A2 | 16 000 | 640 | **256** | 2×2 048 MiB GDDR5 |

(The “Bus Width (bits)” column corresponds to the memory‑bus width; values such as 128, 192, or 256 are taken directly from the table cells.)

*Sources from the page:*  
- “GT 630 … 128” – table cell showing bus width 128.  
- “GT 660 … 192” – table cell showing bus width 192.  
- “GT 660 Ti … 192” – table cell showing bus width 192.  
- “GT 670 … 192” – table cell showing bus width 192.  
- “GT 680 … 192” – table cell showing bus width 192.  
- “GT 690 … 256” – table cell showing bus width 256.  

**Missing**  
The page does not contain any mention of a GeForce GPU that was “known for black screen or BSoD crashes” or any identification of such a model. Consequently, the bus width of the specific “black‑screen/BSOD” GPU cannot be extracted from this page alone.

**Next links**  
The page lists many internal Wikipedia links (e.g., “GeForce GTX 660”, “GeForce GTX 650”, “GeForce GTX 650 Ti”, etc.) and external references. Visiting those pages could provide additional details such as known reliability issues or specific crash reports. No links on the current page specifically promise to resolve the missing fact regarding crash‑susceptible models.

**Status:** partial.
